messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — Sev2 SLA alert for inference-service: tenant=tenant_234 error_rate > 5% for 5m. Link: https://console.redwood/integrations/alerts/1763304000 :rotating_light:

Jamie: ack — I'm oncall, looking. Pulling logs and timeline now.

Miguel: pinged on rotation, I'm nearby if you need a second pair of hands.

Jamie: quick findings — spike in 503/429s from tenant_234 starting 1763303940. Logs show repeated requests with user_agent=synthetic-checker/1.2. Looks like the customer's synthetic healthchecks are hammering the endpoint.

Jamie: logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-16T09:02:32Z inference svc req id=abc tenant=tenant_234 status=503 path=/v1/generate ua=synthetic-checker/1.2 rt=120ms
2026-03-16T09:02:33Z inference svc req id=def tenant=tenant_234 status=503 path=/v1/generate ua=synthetic-checker/1.2 rt=130ms
... repeated ~1200x/minute
```

Sam: infra note — that pattern (burst of identical UA) tends to break our pooling and KV-cache locality; backend threads get saturated. We have some autoscale headroom but the scheduler is slow to react for short bursts.

Priya: support — customer just opened a ticket about periodic failures from their synthetic checks, they thought it was our side. They're on-call too.

Jamie: impact estimate: roughly 18k requests in the 5m window, error rate ~8% for that tenant. That likely counts as an SLA incident for tenant_234 if the contract is 99.9% per 5m window. Marking as potential SLA breach.

Miguel: mitigation options:
- apply a tenant-level rate limit / temp ingress throttle
- add a temporary silence on tenant-scoped SLA alert to avoid noisy pages while we mitigate (we'll still track internally)
- divert tenant to a lower-priority pool if available

Jamie: I'm going to silence the noisy pages for 30m and put a blocking item so we can track SLA exposure. Executing temporary silence now:
```bash
./opsctl alerts silence --service inference-service --filter "tenant:tenant_234" --duration 30m --reason "noisy synthetic checks causing spike"
# returns silence_id=slc-8812
```

Sam: +1 for silence. Also recommend creating a tenant-specific smoothing rule so we don't page on short bursts. We should not change global thresholds.

Miguel: drafting a tenant-scoped alert proposal — to be reviewed: use a longer 'for' period and require higher absolute count to page. Example Prometheus alert snippet: 
```yaml
alert: FinTechTenantHighErrorRate
expr: sum by (tenant) (increase(request_errors_total{service="inference",tenant="tenant_234"}[5m])) / sum by (tenant) (increase(request_total{service="inference",tenant="tenant_234"}[5m])) > 0.07
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
  tenant: tenant_234
annotations:
  summary: "Tenant tenant_234 high error rate (potential SLA)"
  runbook: "https://wiki.redwood/eng/oncall/tenant-alerts"
```

Priya: support — please prepare a customer update: "we're investigating a temporary increase in errors during 09:02-09:07 UTC due to high-volume synthetic checks; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up if there's SLA impact."

Jamie: created internal ticket ENG-3278 "tenant_234 noisy synthetic checks — mitigation + runbook" and assigned Miguel. Adding follow-ups: add synthetic check detection heuristics and tenant-specific rate-limits, update runbook, and schedule a postmortem with support.

Miguel: creating dashboard tiles now: per-tenant error rates, request QPS heatmap, and a synthetic-check detector (UA histogram). Query examples I pushed to Grafana: 
```sql
SELECT tenant, count(*) as errors FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 AND time > now() - 15m GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY errors DESC LIMIT 20;
```

Sam: also adding a circuit-breaker config: if a single tenant's qps > 5000 for >2m and error_rate > 3% then auto-throttle or route to background pool. We'll iterate thresholds after postmortem.

Priya: Support will draft the customer message. If this becomes an SLA breach we'll coordinate formal notification.

Jamie: handoff note — I'm handing off to Miguel at 09:10 UTC. Current state: temp silence active (slc-8812), diverted none yet, autoscale observed small uptick. Watch for reoccurrence.

Miguel: ack taking over. I'll keep the silence until we have smoothing in place and then replace with tenant-scoped alert.

support-bot: Support ticket #44512 updated: customer notified that we're investigating. Tagging for SLA tracking. :white_check_mark:

Jamie: FYI I'll add a short post-incident blurb in #incidents later today with timeline and action items.

Miguel: post-incident action items (summary):
- Implement tenant-specific smoothing alert (ENG-3280)
- Add synthetic-check UA detector and automatic throttle (ENG-3281)
- Update oncall runbook with silence best-practices and tenant handoff steps
- Create customer communication template for potential SLA windows

Priya: support will coordinate postmortem comms and prepare an SLA exposure calc for legal if needed.

Jamie: closing pager for now — still monitoring but noise reduced after silence. If anyone sees another spike, re-page. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Auto-note — this thread will be archived in 30 days.
